experiment: E8 part B: renderer closure of Home Assistant 2026.7.4 on a copy of the real deployment's recorder
what: Why (review R3, W2). The closure the paper prints (fourteen fields) was measured by mutating one state row and one event row of a 43-row demo window (exp/out/e4_closure.json). The real-deployment attempt (exp/out/e4_real_closure.json) ran inside the live hub and aborted after the first event field with "restore did not reproduce the baseline render", after flagging states.last_changed_ts directly. Method. A copy of the default deployment's recorder (SQLite backup API, read-only, taken from hpr-hass) is served to a throwaway hub (container e8b-hass, image homeassistant/home-assistant:2026.7.4, the image hpr-hass runs) whose recorder is disabled once the hub has started, so nothing but this stage writes to the copy. For each target row (several roles: front-door lock, lights, motion sensors, automation runs, service calls, user-bearing rows, rows with and without old_state_id) every stored column of the row and of the states_meta / state_attributes / event_types / event_data row it references is mutated in turn, in one or more variants, through a separate SQLite connection (as code in the hub process can). After each mutation the release's own logbook processor (EventProcessor) renders the target's window (+-300 s) in three request forms: the Activity panel's (no entity filter, websocket form), the entity's own logbook (entity filter, websocket form) and the REST form with names (entity filter). The rendered output is compared byte for byte with the baseline; the rows are aligned to classify the change (row vanished or appeared, displayed cause of a row changed, decoration only, order only); the frontend's display rule (the transcription of home-assistant-frontend 20260624.6 used in exp/out/e_ps_render_reconciliation.json) is applied for an admin and a non-admin viewer; and the commitments of the monitor's closure, stable-columns and row schemes over the window are recomputed with the monitor's own loaders. The mutation is then restored and checked three ways: the stored row equals its original (value and type), every render equals the baseline byte for byte, every commitment equals the baseline. A mutation of the user column is the positive control on every rendered target; rendering the baseline twice is the determinism control. A replay of the earlier harness (homeprov_e4, unchanged) on the frozen copy reproduces the earlier abort when, and only when, a row is written into the window during the measurement.

recorder_copy.method: sqlite3 backup API, mode=ro, in hpr-hass (docker exec hpr-hass python3 -c ...), written to /tmp/e8b_copy.db in the container, docker cp out, then removed
recorder_copy.inner_stdout_fields: (max state_id, max states.event_id [legacy column], max last_updated_ts, max time_fired_ts) seconds bytes finished_epoch
recorder_copy.note: taken by hand with exactly the code in acquire(); /tmp listing of hpr-hass afterwards showed the copy removed

inputs.configuration_yaml:
# Throwaway hub for E8 part B (renderer closure on a copy of the real deployment's recorder).
# Same core configuration as testbed/real/ha-config/configuration.yaml, without the experiment integrations and without
# MQTT; the recorder serves the copy, never purges or repacks it, and is disabled once the hub has started.
homeassistant:
  name: HomeProv Real
  latitude: 0
  longitude: 0
  elevation: 0
  unit_system: metric
  time_zone: UTC

http:
  server_port: 8123

recorder:
  db_url: sqlite:////e8bdb/work.db
  commit_interval: 1
  purge_keep_days: 30
  auto_purge: false
  auto_repack: false

logbook:
history:

automation: !include automations.yaml

logger:
  default: warning

e8b_closure:

forms.activity: EventProcessor(event types for no filter, entity_ids=None, timestamp=True, include_entity_name=False): the Activity panel's websocket request
forms.entity: EventProcessor(event types for the entity, entity_ids=[entity], timestamp=True, include_entity_name=False): the entity's own logbook (websocket)
forms.rest_entity: EventProcessor(..., entity_ids=[entity], timestamp=False, include_entity_name=True): the REST form, as the earlier E4 harness rendered

sql.activity:
SELECT events.event_id AS row_id, event_types.event_type AS event_type, CASE WHEN (event_data.shared_data IS NULL) THEN events.event_data ELSE event_data.shared_data END AS event_data, events.time_fired_ts AS time_fired_ts, events.context_id_bin AS context_id_bin, events.context_user_id_bin AS context_user_id_bin, events.context_parent_id_bin AS context_parent_id_bin, ? AS state, ? AS entity_id, ? AS icon, ? AS attributes, ? AS context_only 
FROM events LEFT OUTER JOIN event_types ON events.event_type_id = event_types.event_type_id LEFT OUTER JOIN event_data ON events.data_id = event_data.data_id 
WHERE events.time_fired_ts > ? AND events.time_fired_ts < ? AND events.event_type_id IN (__[POSTCOMPILE_event_type_ids_1]) UNION ALL SELECT states.state_id AS row_id, ? AS event_type, ? AS event_data, states.last_updated_ts AS time_fired_ts, states.context_id_bin AS context_id_bin, states.context_user_id_bin AS context_user_id_bin, states.context_parent_id_bin AS context_parent_id_bin, states.state AS state, states_meta.entity_id AS entity_id, CASE WHEN (JSON_QUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(CAST(state_attributes.shared_attrs AS TEXT), ?)) IS NULL) THEN JSON_EXTRACT(CAST(states.attributes AS TEXT), ?) ELSE JSON_EXTRACT(CAST(state_attributes.shared_attrs AS TEXT), ?) END AS icon, CASE WHEN (state_attributes.shared_attrs IS NULL) THEN states.attributes ELSE state_attributes.shared_attrs END AS attributes, ? AS context_only 
FROM states LEFT OUTER JOIN states AS old_state ON states.old_state_id = old_state.state_id LEFT OUTER JOIN state_attributes ON states.attributes_id = state_attributes.attributes_id LEFT OUTER JOIN states_meta ON states.metadata_id = states_meta.metadata_id 
WHERE states.last_updated_ts > ? AND states.last_updated_ts < ? AND old_state.state_id IS NOT NULL AND states.state != old_state.state AND states.state IS NOT NULL AND ((states_meta.entity_id NOT LIKE ? AND states_meta.entity_id NOT LIKE ? AND states_meta.entity_id NOT LIKE ? AND states_meta.entity_id NOT LIKE ?) OR ((states_meta.entity_id LIKE ?) AND (state_attributes.shared_attrs NOT LIKE ? OR states.attributes NOT LIKE ?))) AND (states.last_updated_ts = states.last_changed_ts OR states.last_changed_ts IS NULL) ORDER BY time_fired_ts, time_fired_ts
